newsitem.title: USA: Two oil tankers held up by Colombian pipe bombings.
newsitem.headline: Two oil tankers held up by Colombian pipe bombings.

text.p: Two crude oil tankers are held up in the Colombian port of Coveas where they are unable to load as a result of back-to-back rebel bombings of the Cao Limn-Coveas pipeline, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Despite the delay, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol has not declared force majeur on its crude contracts, company soruces said.
Although pipeline bombings are frequent in Colombia, the two recent blasts left little volume in the floating storage unit at Coveas, which has a capacity of two million barrels.
The pipeline is expected to be repaired sometime between Thursday and the weekend, allowing the tankers to load their respective cargoes then.
One tanker, a Panamax vessel named Santa Panaglia, was supposed to load around 400,000 barrels of Cao Limn crude on Tuesday. The tanker was bound for Spain's Repsol in Peru, sources said.
The other tanker, named Harrier, is believed to belong to Shell Oil Co, although this information could not be immediately confirmed.
Occidental Petroleum Corp, which operates the 215,000 barrels per day (bpd) Cao Limn field, was forced to temporarily shut in output after Tuesday's blast, the second in a week.
Ecopetrol operates the damaged pipeline, which carries 200,000 barrels per day of crude the Cao Limon field in northeast Arauca province to the Caribbean port of Coveas.
In all, the pipeline has been blown up 34 times so far this year.
All of the attacks are thought to be the work of National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels, who dynamited the pipeline 47 times last year and spilled more than 105,000 barrels of crude.
